items.claim: Client-side disclosure is mined from shipped JavaScript, which routinely exposes API base URLs, internal hostnames, and commented-out credentials absent from the HTML.
items.body:
In practice on HTB this shows up as: Code deobfuscation is an important skill to learn if we want to be skilled in code analysis and reverse engineering. During red/blue team exercises, we often come across obfuscated code that wants to hide certain functionalities, like malware that utilizes obfuscated JavaScript code to retrieve its main payload. Without understanding what this code is doing, we may not know what exactly the code is doing, and hence may not be able to complete the red/blue team exercise.

Write-up provenance: Esther7171/HackTheBox-Writeups-Walkthroughs :: Write-ups/Academy/01. Pre-Engagement/07. JavaScript Deobfuscation/JavaScript Deobfuscation.md (4818 words, classified web).
items.disproof: Refuted when the shipped bundle contains no internal hostname, key, or credential and every reference is a public endpoint already visible in the HTML.
